people.role: Head of Mục Vân Trang since 1060; horse lord of the western plain
people.appearance: A big, slow, sun-creased man in a felt coat that smells of horse, who looks at people the way he looks at colts, for a long time before he decides.
people.backstory: Khấu Mục Vân was born in Thanh Điền in 940, and a spirit foal was born in the manor's stable the same night; it has let no one else ride it (A169). He called it Đạp Vân, Cloud-Treader. His father Khấu Thường Thanh (khau_thuong_thanh) was a herder of the manor, the one Lạc Hà's treasurer Trầm Tịch Dương (tram_tich_duong) shorted three stones at the horse fair of 901, the day the market girl Tô Vãn Chiếu said so in front of them both. The founder Mẫn Bạch Câu (man_bach_cau) taught Khấu the long ride and left him the manor in 1060. In the cold year of 1121 the herds died in the snow (A171, V100), and Lạc Hà's Counting House would not delay the tribute. Since then Khấu has paid it every year less three stones and three hundred years of interest at Lạc Hà's own posted rate, citing Lạc Hà's own contract law. The Hall of Scales calls the tribute late. He has had its collector Cận Thủ Chuyết (can_thu_chuyet) thrown off the ranch twice. His horses win every race at the lord's festival (A172).
people.wants: To have the three stones paid back, with interest, by Trầm Tịch Dương's own hand, at a festival, in front of a herder. After that, nothing much.
people.secret: Đạp Vân is failing. Thôi Dương Giác's book told him why a spirit foal born on his night answers only him: the horse's Wind and his are one thread. He expects that when the horse dies, he will not be long behind it, and he has told no one, not even his daughter.

tree.targets_note: The rider's route (Solid Ground, Beast Pen), then Swift Hound, Ten Thousand Beasts One Heart and Beast Soul Union: horse and rider as one body.

people.role: Elder of the manor; the last disciple of Phù Dao Quán, keeper of its Wind book
people.appearance: A narrow, weathered woman who stands facing into the wind out of habit, with a frostbitten left hand she keeps in her sleeve.
people.backstory: Thôi Dương Giác was a well-digger's girl from Song Tỉnh Thôn whom the masters of Phù Dao Quán, the Abbey of the Whirlwind on the steppe, took at seven because she had Wind, the only thing they taught. The abbey had six people left by 1100. In the cold year the herds died, the geese flew low over Nhạn Thanh Thành (A171), and the old master died in his cell with the shutters open to the wind (V100). Thôi, seventy-one and at Trúc Cơ, buried him, took the pennant off the pole and walked three juniors and the abbey's book to the one house on the plain that would feed them. Khấu Mục Vân (khau_muc_van) fed them. Two of the juniors have died since. The third is Mạc Khiên Phong (mac_khien_phong), who has no Wind. She made Kết Đan at the manor in 1160 and has taught the abbey's book to no one, because no one at the manor but its head has Wind, and he has a herd to run.
people.wants: To light the abbey on the steppe again with Wind-born disciples. Lạc Hà looked at Phù Dao Quán for its new seat and passed it over as the vassal's; she wants it given to her in writing.
people.secret: She has written to Phất Y Cốc and Cửu Cao Phái, the Wind sects of the Pivot's lands, offering the abbey's book in exchange for three Wind-born disciples. Selling a vassal's art to the Pivot's vassals without leave is a breach of the manor's oath to Lạc Hà.

people.role: Herd master: the breeding herds, the remounts and the long ride
people.appearance: A bow-legged herder with a split lip from a mare's hoof and hands like saddle leather.
people.backstory: A flute-village herder's son from Mục Địch Thôn who rode the long ride at sixteen and never got off. He saw the herds die in the snow of 1121 (A171) and has built them back colt by colt. Khấu Mục Vân (khau_muc_van) means him to run the herds after him. Tần believes the white bear in the north paddock is upsetting the mares, and he is right. He does not watch the old mares go.

people.role: Steward of the manor; keeps the herd books and the tribute ledger
people.appearance: A broad, quiet woman with ink on her cuffs and a reed pen behind her ear.
people.backstory: Khấu Mục Vân's (khau_muc_van) daughter, born in the stables, and the one who worked out the sum: three stones shorted in 901 at Lạc Hà's posted rate for late debts come to nearly five thousand by 1200, more than a year's tribute. She sends the Hall of Scales a corrected account every spring, signed and sealed at sunset as Lạc Hà's law requires. Từ Bình Hành has not yet found the error, because there is none.

people.role: The manor's race rider; won every race at the lord's festival in 1185
people.appearance: A wiry, grinning rider of thirty-five with a broken nose and a festival ribbon braided into her hair every day of the year.
people.backstory: A Thảo Đường Thành stable orphan who came to the manor to muck out and stayed to ride. At twenty she won every race at the lord's festival of 1185 (A172), and Kim Vạn Lý (kim_van_ly) lost his bet anyway, because he bet on her losing one. She wants to race Lạc Hà's Geese Hall cadets on their own drill field, and Thôi Dương Giác (thoi_duong_giac) has been teaching her to read the wind on the course. She rules her own races, moving the finishing post a length after the heat when the wind turns, and Kim Vạn Lý has lost three bets to her rulings.

people.backstory: A Thanh Điền herder who gathered the plain's horse families into one manor in 740 to breed spirit horses that run like clouds (A166), and wrote the body canon from the way they broke colts. He gave Lạc Hà remounts for Chiết Kích Nguyên and lost most of them there (N-muc_van-01). He rode out on his last long ride in 1060 and the horse came back without him. He left the manor to Khấu Mục Vân (khau_muc_van).
